mechanism: transfection of the active NF-kappaB subunit p65 (RELA) raises Orai1 transcript in mast cells of either sgk1 genotype, and p65 with p50 or p52 does so in HEK293 cells; luciferase assays and chromatin immunoprecipitation then located NF-kappaB binding sites in the Orai1 and STIM1 promoter regions. RELA is this curator's reading of "p65": the paper names the subunits it transfects, so the isoform is the paper's, not an interpretation
sentence: Orai1 and STIM1 transcript levels were further increased in sgk1(+/+) and sgk1(-/-) mast cells by transfection with active NF-kappaB subunit p65 as well as in HEK293 cells by transfection with NF-kappaB subunits p65/p50 or p65/p52.
justification: The first NF-kappaB record the map can carry, because this paper names p65, p50 and p52 instead of writing "NF-kappaB". It is also the upstream direction: the transcription factor setting how much channel exists, with promoter binding sites to support it.

mechanism: same transfections and the same chromatin immunoprecipitation of the STIM1 promoter region
sentence: Orai1 and STIM1 transcript levels were further increased in sgk1(+/+) and sgk1(-/-) mast cells by transfection with active NF-kappaB subunit p65 as well as in HEK293 cells by transfection with NF-kappaB subunits p65/p50 or p65/p52.
justification: The sensor side of the same promoter regulation, so the transcription factor sits above the pair rather than above one of them.

mechanism: the functional consequence of the same overexpression: store-operated Ca2+ entry rises with p65/p50 or p65/p52 and falls under the NF-kappaB inhibitor wogonin, and migration follows the same pattern
sentence: Store-operated Ca(2+) entry was similarly increased by overexpression of p65/p50 or p65/p52 and decreased by treatment with Wogonin.
justification: The expression change reaches the current, which is what makes the promoter result relevant to the map rather than a transcriptomic aside.

mechanism: Orai1 transcript falls in mast cells from sgk1 knock-out mice and rises in HEK293 cells transfected with active (S422D)SGK1 but not with the inactive (K127N) kinase; the NF-kappaB inhibitor wogonin abolishes the effect, placing NF-kappaB between the kinase and the promoter
sentence: Orai1 and STIM1 transcript levels were decreased in mast cells from SGK1 knock-out mice and increased in HEK293 cells transfected with active (S422D)SGK1 but not with inactive (K127N)SGK1 or in (S422D)SGK1-transfected cells treated with the NF-kappaB inhibitor Wogonin (100 mum).
justification: SGK1 is one of the curator's rows; this is the publication under it, with a knock-out, a kinase-dead control and the intermediate (NF-kappaB) identified.

mechanism: same knock-out and kinase-dead comparison; stem cell factor raises STIM1 and Orai1 transcripts in sgk1(+/+) but not sgk1(-/-) mast cells, and not under wogonin
sentence: Orai1 and STIM1 transcript levels were decreased in mast cells from SGK1 knock-out mice and increased in HEK293 cells transfected with active (S422D)SGK1 but not with inactive (K127N)SGK1 or in (S422D)SGK1-transfected cells treated with the NF-kappaB inhibitor Wogonin (100 mum).
justification: The sensor side of the SGK1 row, completing a two-step upstream path (SGK1 -> NF-kappaB -> anchors) that the map can now draw with named proteins.

mechanism: independent replication in a different lineage: transfecting p50/p65 into megakaryocytic MEG-01 cells raises STIM1 and Orai1 transcript and protein by 46-97%
sentence: Transfection with p50/p65 significantly increased STIM1/Orai1 transcript and protein levels in megakaryocytic MEG-01 cells (by 46-97%).
justification: A second, unrelated laboratory and cell type reaching the same conclusion as PMID 22110130, which is what makes the NF-kappaB -> anchors direction solid enough to record despite the family naming problem.

mechanism: same MEG-01 transfection
sentence: Transfection with p50/p65 significantly increased STIM1/Orai1 transcript and protein levels in megakaryocytic MEG-01 cells (by 46-97%).
justification: The channel side of the replication.

mechanism: klotho-deficient (kl/kl) mice have excessive 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D3; their platelets and megakaryocytes show STIM1/Orai1 transcript and protein, SOCE, CRAC current, degranulation, integrin alphaIIbbeta3 activation and thrombus formation all blunted by 27-90%, and treating wild-type megakaryocytes with 1,25(OH)2D3 reproduces it
sentence: Klotho deficiency inhibits platelet Ca(2+) signaling and activation, an effect at least partially due to 1,25(OH)2D3-dependent down-regulation of NF-kappaB activity and STIM1/Orai1 expression in megakaryocytes.
justification: An endocrine input two steps above the anchors (klotho -> vitamin D3 -> NF-kappaB -> STIM1/Orai1) with a whole-animal read-out, thrombus formation. It is the first hormonal regulator of anchor abundance in the map.

mechanism: same klotho-deficient mice and the same vitamin D3 treatment of wild-type megakaryocytes
sentence: Klotho deficiency inhibits platelet Ca(2+) signaling and activation, an effect at least partially due to 1,25(OH)2D3-dependent down-regulation of NF-kappaB activity and STIM1/Orai1 expression in megakaryocytes.
justification: The channel side of the klotho arm.

mechanism: blastocyst-secreted proteases acting on PAR2 (F2RL1) start Ca2+ oscillations in mouse endometrial epithelial cells; the Orai1 blocker YM58483 prevents the oscillations while leaving the initial release intact, so PAR2 reaches the channel through PLC and IP3R
sentence: In addition, this study unraveled the molecular players involved in the downstream signaling of PAR2 by showing that depletion and re-filling of intracellular calcium stores occurs via PLC, IP3R and the STIM1/Orai1 complex.
justification: The PAR2 half of a contrast the map now holds completely: batch 14 recorded F2RL3 (PAR4) -> ORAI1 from the house dust mite protease, where PAR2 was explicitly the receptor Ca2+ influx was *not* coupled to. Here, with a different protease source, PAR2 does reach the channel - so the receptor isoform that matters depends on the stimulus, and both are named.

mechanism: same pharmacology; the oscillations need store depletion and refilling through the STIM1/Orai1 complex
sentence: In addition, this study unraveled the molecular players involved in the downstream signaling of PAR2 by showing that depletion and re-filling of intracellular calcium stores occurs via PLC, IP3R and the STIM1/Orai1 complex.
justification: The sensor side of the PAR2 input, in a physiological setting (embryo implantation) rather than a cell line.

mechanism: immunoprecipitation shows PKC-beta binding the Stim1 C terminus and phosphorylating it in vitro, with Ser660 as the important target site; the S660A mutant has a higher basal SOCE and no longer responds to the PKC activator PMA
sentence: Using immunoprecipitation and Ca2+ mobilization and confocal assays, we discovered that (1) PKC-beta interacts with and phosphorylates the C-terminal region of Stim1, whereby residue Ser660 represents an important target site, (2) mutation of Ser660 to Ala restores SOCE activity in response to PKC activation, (3) PKC activity is inversely related to SOCE activity, and (4) Stim1 oligomerization induced by ionomycin is affected by either chemical activators or inhibitors of PKC isozymes.
justification: PRKCB is one of the curator's rows and this is the publication under it, with the isoform named, the residue named and a phospho-null control. It also gives the map a second kinase on STIM1 beside DYRK2 (batch 12).

mechanism: the functional direction of the same phosphorylation: PKC activity is inversely related to SOCE, PKC inhibits Stim1 puncta formation after store depletion, and the authors read it as de-oligomerization of Stim1
sentence: Using immunoprecipitation and Ca2+ mobilization and confocal assays, we discovered that (1) PKC-beta interacts with and phosphorylates the C-terminal region of Stim1, whereby residue Ser660 represents an important target site, (2) mutation of Ser660 to Ala restores SOCE activity in response to PKC activation, (3) PKC activity is inversely related to SOCE activity, and (4) Stim1 oligomerization induced by ionomycin is affected by either chemical activators or inhibitors of PKC isozymes.
justification: Recorded separately from the phosphorylation because the sign matters: most kinases reported on STIM1 (ERK, PKA, PAK) raise SOCE, and this one lowers it, so the map should not leave the reader to guess.

mechanism: co-immunoprecipitation of Orai1 with the large-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channel; the interaction is reduced in diabetic mice even though Orai1 protein is raised, and suppressing Orai1 or blocking BKCa both increase agonist-induced contraction, so the complex normally brakes contraction
sentence: Conclusion: We concluded that the increased SOCE caused by excessive STIM1 and Orai1 expression and decreased Orai1-BKCa interaction augmented small intestinal smooth muscle contraction and accelerated small bowel transit speed in diabetic mice.
justification: A potassium channel physically coupled to ORAI1, so Ca2+ entry is read directly into membrane potential. It also explains how more channel can mean more contraction: the amount of ORAI1 and its partnership with BKCa move in opposite directions in disease.

mechanism: transgenic STIM1 overexpression in mouse heart: myocytes show spontaneous Ca2+ transients that SKF-96365 prevents, a larger L-type current and more Ca2+ sparks, with cardiomyopathy in vivo. CACNA1C is this curator's reading of "L-type Ca2+ channel" in ventricular myocytes, where the current is carried by Cav1.2 - the paper itself writes only LTCC
sentence: Mechanistically, cardiac myocytes isolated from STIM1 transgenic mice displayed spontaneous Ca(2+) transients that were prevented by the SOCE blocker SKF-96365, increased L-type Ca(2+) channel (LTCC) current, and enhanced Ca(2+) spark frequency.
justification: Opposite in sign to the STIM1 -> CACNA1C inhibition recorded in batch 13 (PMID 20929813, where the SOAR domain suppresses Cav1.2 in smooth muscle and HEK cells), so the map pairs them as a conflict: gain of STIM1 in cardiac muscle raises the L-type current, direct SOAR binding in smooth muscle lowers it.

mechanism: the same transgenic hearts: STIM1 partially co-localizes with the type 2 ryanodine receptor in the sarcoplasmic reticulum and Ca2+ spark frequency is enhanced, with spontaneous transients abolished by a SOCE blocker
sentence: Mechanistically, cardiac myocytes isolated from STIM1 transgenic mice displayed spontaneous Ca(2+) transients that were prevented by the SOCE blocker SKF-96365, increased L-type Ca(2+) channel (LTCC) current, and enhanced Ca(2+) spark frequency.
justification: The cardiac release channel under STIM1, with the isoform named by the paper (RyR2). Sparks are RyR2 events, so the functional claim is the sign of this edge; the co-localization is only circumstantial and is left in the mechanism.

mechanism: the muscular-hypotonia mutant STIM1 R429C binds endogenous STIM1 and acts as a dominant negative: it raises depolarization-evoked Ca2+ movement by removing the attenuation that endogenous STIM1 exerts on DHPR-RyR1 coupling, while also slowing the initial rate of SOCE
sentence: Moreover, R429C increased intracellular Ca2+ movement in response to membrane depolarization by eliminating the attenuation on dihydropyridine receptor-ryanodine receptor (DHPR-RyR1) coupling by endogenous STIM1.
justification: A second, non-SOCE job for STIM1 in skeletal muscle: it holds back excitation-contraction coupling. The sign is read from a dominant-negative mutant, which is cleaner than overexpression, and it sets up the STIM1/STIM2 split over SERCA1a recorded below.

mechanism: same dominant-negative experiment; the authors propose the mutant's oligomerization interferes with the binding between endogenous STIM1 and DHPR. CACNA1S is this curator's reading of "dihydropyridine receptor" in skeletal myotubes, where the DHPR alpha1 subunit is Cav1.1 - the paper writes only DHPR
sentence: Moreover, R429C increased intracellular Ca2+ movement in response to membrane depolarization by eliminating the attenuation on dihydropyridine receptor-ryanodine receptor (DHPR-RyR1) coupling by endogenous STIM1.
justification: Completes the pair STIM1 brakes in skeletal muscle. With CACNA1C in cardiac muscle and CACNA1S here, the map now shows STIM1 touching both voltage-gated channels, and both resolutions of a generic channel name are flagged in the mechanism.

mechanism: manipulating the junctional lipid transfer proteins at ER/PM junctions: ORP5 inhibits STIM1 clustering and the STIM1-Orai1 interaction, and co-expressing Orai1 rescues the clustering while displacing ORP5 from the junctions; targeting the PtdSer-hydrolysing PLA1a1 to the ER reproduces the inhibition, so the effect runs through ER phosphatidylserine
sentence: While ORP5 inhibits, ORP8 facilitates STIM1-STIM1 and STIM1-Orai1 interactions, Orai1 current, and the receptor-stimulated Ca2+ oscillations.
justification: The ORPs were on the map's blocked list as a family name; this paper names ORP5 and ORP8 and gives them opposite signs, which is exactly why the family could not be recorded as one node. It also adds lipid composition - the PtdSer/PI(4)P ratio - as a regulator of the anchors' coupling.

mechanism: same experiments; the ORPs do not act on Orai1 conductance directly (the current from Orai1 activated by a free SOAR domain is unaffected), only through STIM1 clustering
sentence: While ORP5 inhibits, ORP8 facilitates STIM1-STIM1 and STIM1-Orai1 interactions, Orai1 current, and the receptor-stimulated Ca2+ oscillations.
justification: The current is the read-out the physiology depends on, and the mechanism note records what the paper excluded: no direct lipid regulation of the pore.

mechanism: ORP8 facilitates STIM1 self-association and STIM1-Orai1 interaction; STIM1 increases ORP8 clustering upon ER Ca2+ depletion, and targeting PLA1a1 to the plasma membrane mimics ORP8
sentence: While ORP5 inhibits, ORP8 facilitates STIM1-STIM1 and STIM1-Orai1 interactions, Orai1 current, and the receptor-stimulated Ca2+ oscillations.
justification: The paralogue with the opposite sign, from the same experiments in the same cells - the cleanest possible argument against collapsing a protein family into one node.

mechanism: same experiments; when Ca2+ influx is inhibited ORP8 can raise plasma membrane PI(4)P and the PI(4)P/PtdSer ratio to facilitate STIM1 clustering and increase the Orai1 current
sentence: While ORP5 inhibits, ORP8 facilitates STIM1-STIM1 and STIM1-Orai1 interactions, Orai1 current, and the receptor-stimulated Ca2+ oscillations.
justification: The channel side of the ORP8 arm.

mechanism: knocking down SAP97 (DLG1) in Jurkat cells, or deleting the Orai1 N terminus, makes Orai1 keep accumulating at the immunological synapse up to 60 minutes instead of leaving it; SOCE and membrane targeting are preserved, but the Ca2+ response to CD3-CD28 beads becomes persistently oscillatory
sentence: Ca2+-signaling of IS engaged cells was vastly different: cells with sustained Orai1 IS-accumulation (Jurkat cells expressing N-terminal mutant Orai1 or Orai1-Full in SAP97 knocked-down Jurkat cells) displayed oscillatory Ca2+-response up to the 90th minute after IS formation unlike control cells.
justification: A trafficking edge whose consequence is the *shape* of the calcium signal rather than its size - the first record in the map where removing a partner leaves SOCE intact and changes only the oscillation pattern. It matters for T cell activation, where duration is the message.

mechanism: SAP97 binds the Orai1 N terminus, and the interaction requires STIM1 binding to that same N-terminal region; the authors propose Orai1 is guided out of the synapse as a complex with STIM1 and SAP97
sentence: Overall, these data suggest that SAP97 may contribute to the short-lived IS-residency of Orai1 and binding of STIM1 to Orai1 N-terminus is necessary for SAP97-Orai1 interaction.
justification: The contact behind the trafficking edge, and a dependency worth keeping: the scaffold needs STIM1 already on the channel, so this is a three-body arrangement rather than two independent partners.

mechanism: leptin raises SOCE and Orai1 expression in dendritic cells from mouse bone marrow, and the effects of leptin on migration and maturation are lost without Orai1
sentence: Firstly, we confirmed the positive effects of leptin upon SOCE and Orai1 expression in DCs isolated from mouse bone marrow.
justification: A metabolic hormone upstream of ORAI1 abundance in antigen-presenting cells - the kind of link that connects the map's immune arm to whole-body metabolism, which the TRPC1 -> ADIPOQ record of batch 14 also touches from the other side.

mechanism: exposing ovary carcinoma cells to placental growth factor raised Orai1 and STIM1 transcript and protein and increased store-operated entry, an effect abolished by the Orai1 inhibitor MRS1845
sentence: In conclusion, PlGF upregulates expression of both, Orai1 and STIM1 thus enhancing store-operated Ca2+-entry with subsequent upregulation of HIF1alpha.
justification: A tumour-derived growth factor raising the abundance of both anchors, with the channel blocker showing the rise is functional. It is the input half of a loop whose output (HIF1A) is recorded next.

mechanism: same exposure; both transcripts and both proteins rise
sentence: In conclusion, PlGF upregulates expression of both, Orai1 and STIM1 thus enhancing store-operated Ca2+-entry with subsequent upregulation of HIF1alpha.
justification: The sensor side of the growth factor input.

mechanism: HIF1alpha transcript and protein rise downstream of the PlGF-driven increase in SOCE; the authors place HIF1alpha after the Ca2+ entry step rather than beside it
sentence: In conclusion, PlGF upregulates expression of both, Orai1 and STIM1 thus enhancing store-operated Ca2+-entry with subsequent upregulation of HIF1alpha.
justification: The hypoxia master regulator downstream of ORAI1 gives the map a transcription factor that is neither NFAT nor NF-kappaB, and one whose targets (angiogenesis, glycolysis) fit the tumour phenotypes several other records in the map end at.

mechanism: same chain, with STIM1 raised alongside Orai1 by placental growth factor
sentence: In conclusion, PlGF upregulates expression of both, Orai1 and STIM1 thus enhancing store-operated Ca2+-entry with subsequent upregulation of HIF1alpha.
justification: The sensor side of the HIF1A arm; the paper does not separate the two anchors here, and the record says so by carrying the same sentence.

mechanism: inhibiting or knocking down Ca2+-independent phospholipase A2 beta (iPLA2beta, PLA2G6) causes a dramatic loss of *endogenous* SOCE in HEK293 cells; overexpressing either Orai1 or STIM1 masks that requirement, and there is cross-talk between Orai1 expression and a plasma-membrane variant of iPLA2beta but not STIM1
sentence: Although functional inhibition of Ca(2+)-independent phospholipase A(2) beta (iPLA(2)beta or PLA2g6A), or depletion of plasma membrane cholesterol caused a dramatic loss of endogenous SOCE in HEK293 cells, these effects were attenuated significantly when either Orai1 or STIM1 were overexpressed.
justification: A regulator that is only visible at endogenous expression levels - a warning the map should carry explicitly, since most of its edges come from overexpression experiments that would have hidden this one.

mechanism: remifentanil raises STIM1 and Orai1 in the rat spinal dorsal horn and CaMKIIalpha phosphorylation with them; intrathecal YM-58483 suppresses the phosphorylation without changing STIM1 or Orai1 levels, so the channel activity and not the protein amount carries the signal
sentence: The over-expressed STIM1 and Orai1 in the spinal cord contribute to RIPH via mediating the phosphorylation of CaMKIIalpha.
justification: CaMKII has been on the map's blocked list because papers write the family name; this one writes CaMKIIalpha, so a level-2 seed of the curator's effector module finally gets a literature edge from an anchor, with a pharmacological control.

mechanism: same model and the same blocker experiment
sentence: The over-expressed STIM1 and Orai1 in the spinal cord contribute to RIPH via mediating the phosphorylation of CaMKIIalpha.
justification: The channel side of the CaMKIIalpha edge, in a pain model where the behavioural read-out (hyperalgesia) follows the phosphorylation.

mechanism: TRIC-A is recruited by STIM1 into ER-PM junction punctae after store depletion and interacts with it; the recruitment depends on the interaction with STIM1 rather than on TRIC-A's own ER Ca2+ sensing, and STIM1-D76A clusters it constitutively
sentence: Together, the data in Figs 5 and 6 indicate that TRIC-A interacts with STIM1 and is recruited by STIM1 to ER-PM junctions.
justification: TMEM38A is one of the curator's rows, and this is the publication under it: the partner is STIM1 itself and the contact is what brings the channel to the junction.

mechanism: FRET and normalized FRET show TRIC-A reducing STIM1-Orai1 coupling; Mander's coefficient, puncta size and junctional footprint all fall, protein levels do not change, and ICRAC, SOCE and the frequency of Ca2+ oscillations are attenuated
sentence: Upon ER Ca2+ depletion, TRIC-A clusters with stromal interaction molecule 1 (STIM1) and Ca2+-release-activated Ca2+ channel 1 (Orai1) within ER-plasma membrane (PM) junctions and impairs assembly of the STIM1/Orai1 complex, causing a decrease in Orai1-mediated Ca2+ current and SOCE.
justification: A negative regulator that works by getting between the two anchors, like SARAF (already in the map) and unlike CRACR2A from batch 14, which holds them together. The map now has both signs of junctional third parties.

mechanism: same measurements; TRIC-A interferes with STIM1 clustering and its coupling to Orai1 without changing STIM1 expression
sentence: Upon ER Ca2+ depletion, TRIC-A clusters with stromal interaction molecule 1 (STIM1) and Ca2+-release-activated Ca2+ channel 1 (Orai1) within ER-plasma membrane (PM) junctions and impairs assembly of the STIM1/Orai1 complex, causing a decrease in Orai1-mediated Ca2+ current and SOCE.
justification: The sensor side of the same interference, recorded because the binding edge above says only that they touch, not what the contact does.

mechanism: expressing the active Notch1 intracellular domain (N1ICD) in triple-negative MDA-MB-231 cells lowers Orai1 and Orai3 protein without changing STIM1; SOCE does not change detectably but caspase-3 activation rises. The gamma-secretase inhibitor DAPT has no effect here, suggesting little resting Notch1 activity
sentence: In TNBC MDA-MB-231 cells, a cell line characterized by its high metastatic potential, expression of the active form of Notch1 significantly reduced both Orai1 and Orai3 expression, but not STIM1 protein level, which resulted in no detectable change in SOCE but increased caspase-3 activation, indicating the induction of apoptosis, a pathway that might, at least partially, explain the induction of apoptosis by Notch1.
justification: NOTCH1 is one of the curator's rows and this is the publication under it. It is also a developmental receptor setting the abundance of the ORAI family, which no other record in the map does.

mechanism: same N1ICD expression in MDA-MB-231 cells; Orai3 falls with Orai1
sentence: In TNBC MDA-MB-231 cells, a cell line characterized by its high metastatic potential, expression of the active form of Notch1 significantly reduced both Orai1 and Orai3 expression, but not STIM1 protein level, which resulted in no detectable change in SOCE but increased caspase-3 activation, indicating the induction of apoptosis, a pathway that might, at least partially, explain the induction of apoptosis by Notch1.
justification: ORAI3 matters on its own in luminal breast cancer and B cells, so its regulation is not a by-product of the ORAI1 result.

mechanism: the same construct in the other triple-negative line, BT20, which has lower metastatic potential: N1ICD raises Orai1 and Orai3 protein and increases SOCE. The authors conclude Notch1 can suppress or enhance ORAI expression in a cell-type-specific way
sentence: By contrast, in the TNBC BT20 cell line, which exhibits lower metastatic potential, N1ICD enhanced Orai1 and Orai3 protein levels and increased SOCE.
justification: A conflict in sign that comes from a single paper and a single construct, with only the cell line changing - the cleanest demonstration the map can show that an edge's sign can be contextual rather than contested, and the conflict badge here points at biology, not at a disagreement between laboratories.

mechanism: same BT20 experiment
sentence: By contrast, in the TNBC BT20 cell line, which exhibits lower metastatic potential, N1ICD enhanced Orai1 and Orai3 protein levels and increased SOCE.
justification: The ORAI3 half of the same reversal, so both channels carry the two signs.

mechanism: in non-tumoral MCF10A breast epithelial cells, N1ICD leaves Orai1 and Orai3 untouched but lowers STIM1, so the target of Notch1 inside the SOCE machinery itself depends on whether the cell is tumoral
sentence: In non-tumoral MCF10A cells, N1ICD expression did not induce any detectable modification in Orai1 or Orai3 protein levels, although we detected a reduction in STIM1 expression.
justification: The non-tumoral control, which is where the sensor rather than the channel responds. Keeping it stops the Notch1 arm from reading as a cancer-only phenomenon.

mechanism: HEY1 is induced by Notch1 activation and reproduces its effect on Orai1 and Orai3 in MCF10A, MDA-MB-231 and MCF7 cells; the phosphomimetic HEY1 S68D mutant cannot repress them, unlike wild type and the non-phosphorylatable S68A, so phosphorylation at Ser-68 switches the repression off
sentence: At least in MDA-MB-231 cells, the underlying mechanism for the regulation of Orai channels by Notch1 involves a transcriptional pathway where Notch1 activation leads to the expression of HEY1, which in turn acts as a direct or indirect transcriptional repressor of the genes encoding Orai1 and Orai3.
justification: The transcriptional repressor between NOTCH1 and the channels, with a phospho-site that controls whether it works. It turns a receptor-to-channel correlation into a two-step mechanism the map can draw.

mechanism: the authors name the axis they establish - Notch1 to HEY1 to the Orai channels - and tie it to SOCE; kept as a second evidence row because the substantive sentence above names no calcium term, and the map's inclusion rule needs one somewhere on the node
sentence: Given the important functional role of Orai1 and SOCE in the development of breast cancer hallmarks, including proliferation, migration and metastasis, the analysis of the Notch1-HEY1-Orai axis might provide insights that may ultimately contribute to the development of subtype-specific therapeutic strategies targeting Notch-Orai signaling in breast cancer.
justification: The sentence that states the axis as a whole, and the one that carries the calcium criterion for HEY1. Without it the repressor would be dropped from the map although it is the mechanism of the NOTCH1 edges.

mechanism: same experiments and the same S68 dependence
sentence: At least in MDA-MB-231 cells, the underlying mechanism for the regulation of Orai channels by Notch1 involves a transcriptional pathway where Notch1 activation leads to the expression of HEY1, which in turn acts as a direct or indirect transcriptional repressor of the genes encoding Orai1 and Orai3.
justification: The second channel gene under the same repressor.

mechanism: high-concentrate feeding of mid-lactating cows raised STIM1, ORAI1, PKCalpha, IKKbeta, phospho-IkappaBalpha, phospho-p65, TNF-alpha and IL-1alpha together in mammary tissue, with ER stress and apoptosis. This is co-regulation in vivo with no loss-of-function control, so the direction follows the authors' reading of the pathway rather than an intervention
sentence: The upregulation of STIM1, ORAI1, PKCalpha, IKKbeta, phosphorylated-IkappaBalpha, phosphorylated-p65, TNF-alpha, and IL-1alpha proteins in the HC group indicated activation of the STIM1/ORAI1-mediated inflammatory signaling pathway compared with that in the LC group.
justification: The downstream direction of the NF-kappaB relationship, and the only paper so far that names the subunit (phospho-p65) on that side. It does not settle the sign conflict between PMC4530453 and PMID 36334371, because those two write only "NF-kappaB", but it does mean the map can show at least one named arrow from an anchor to RELA.

mechanism: same in vivo co-regulation, with the same caveat: no knockdown, and the intermediate steps (PKCalpha, IKKbeta, IkappaBalpha) are inferred from phosphorylation state
sentence: The upregulation of STIM1, ORAI1, PKCalpha, IKKbeta, phosphorylated-IkappaBalpha, phosphorylated-p65, TNF-alpha, and IL-1alpha proteins in the HC group indicated activation of the STIM1/ORAI1-mediated inflammatory signaling pathway compared with that in the LC group.
justification: The channel side of the same arrow; PRKCA between them is already in the map from the ventilator-injury paper of batch 14, so the two records join into a path.

mechanism: knocking out STIM2 in colorectal cancer lines activates cMyc and the PERK/ATF4 branch of ER stress, drives glycolysis and GLUT1, and increases tumour growth and metastasis in xenografts; none of it happens in STIM1 KO, Orai1 KO or Orai triple-KO cells, so the arm is Orai-independent
sentence: Mechanistically, STIM2 loss activates cMyc and the PERK/ATF4 branch of ER stress in an Orai-independent manner.
justification: PERK is already in the map under STIM1 (PMID 23076152, batch 14, where losing STIM1 raises PERK and NRF2); here losing STIM2 does the same thing to PERK while losing STIM1 does not. Two sensors, the same ER stress kinase, and an explicit dissociation from the channel.

mechanism: two-dimensional blue native PAGE and co-immunoprecipitation from freshly isolated adult rat ventricular myocytes, where endogenous STIM1 sits along the Z-disk in a large complex at the junctional SR; there is no store-operated entry in these cells at all, and the authors note the action is independent of SOCE
sentence: These changes in Ca(2+) signaling in the SR appear to be due to STIM1 binding to phospholamban and thereby indirectly activating SERCA2a (Sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+) ATPase).
justification: The lead behind a passing mention in PMC10592933, chased to its primary paper. PLN is one of the curator's rows and had no literature edge; this gives it one, and it is a STIM1 function in a cell type that has no SOCE - the clearest case yet that the sensor does more than open ORAI1.

mechanism: indirect, through phospholamban: STIM1 overexpression raises SR Ca2+ content and SR Ca2+ leak in ventricular myocytes without any store-operated entry, and the authors attribute it to relief of phospholamban inhibition of SERCA2a
sentence: These changes in Ca(2+) signaling in the SR appear to be due to STIM1 binding to phospholamban and thereby indirectly activating SERCA2a (Sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+) ATPase).
justification: Batch 13 recorded ATP2A2 -> STIM1 inhibition (the full store keeps the sensor off); this closes the loop in the other direction, with the pump and the sensor regulating each other through phospholamban.

mechanism: binding assays and quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry mapped the contact to STIM1 residues 449-671 (the STIM1-SBR region), and co-immunoprecipitation plus immunocytochemistry confirmed it on endogenous full-length STIM1 in rabbit skeletal muscle and mouse primary myotubes
sentence: STIM1 binds to sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase 1a (SERCA1a) via this region (called STIM1-SBR).
justification: The skeletal-muscle counterpart of the cardiac phospholamban result, and on a different region of STIM1 from the one that activates ORAI1 - so the sensor's C terminus carries at least two separable jobs.

mechanism: STIM1 knockdown in mouse primary myotubes lowered Ca2+ uptake into the SR through SERCA1a, but only at micromolar cytosolic Ca2+, and expressing the isolated STIM1-SBR region shifted intracellular Ca2+ distribution without affecting SOCE
sentence: STIM1 knockdown in mouse primary skeletal myotubes decreased Ca2+ uptake from the cytosol to the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) through SERCA1a only at micromolar cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations, suggesting that STIM1 could be required for the full activity of SERCA1a possibly during the relaxation of skeletal muscle.
justification: The functional sign of the contact, with the condition attached: the requirement only shows at high cytosolic Ca2+, i.e. during relaxation. Conditions like that are what the map's mechanism field exists for.

mechanism: binding assay, mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation from rabbit skeletal muscle expressing bona-fide STIM2 and SERCA1a; the contact is made by STIM2 residues 453-729, the region corresponding to the STIM1-SBR
sentence: The region for amino acids from 453 to 729 of STIM2 binds to sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase 1a (SERCA1a).
justification: The homologous contact from the homologous sensor, chased from the same lead. It sets up the comparison that follows, where the two sensors bind the same pump through the same region and do opposite things to it.

mechanism: oxalate-supported 45Ca2+ uptake and single-myotube imaging in STIM2-knockdown mouse primary myotubes: STIM2 attenuates SERCA1a activity during contraction, which sets the resting distribution of Ca2+ between cytosol and SR. STIM1 does the opposite through the same binding region, which the authors describe as a tug of war
sentence: STIM2 binds to SERCA1a via its C-terminal region of amino acids from 453 to 729, and attenuates SERCA1a activity during skeletal muscle contraction.
justification: Two homologous sensors with opposite signs on the same pump, each with its own binding region mapped. The map cannot show this as a conflict - the sources differ - but it is the strongest case in the batch for keeping STIM1 and STIM2 apart, which the curator's inclusion rule already does.

mechanism: disrupting the STIM-SERCA1a interaction changes release through RyR1 in opposite directions for the two sensors: Ca2+ movement through RyR1 fell when the STIM1-SERCA1a interaction was disrupted and rose when the STIM2-SERCA1a interaction was, so the effect on RyR1 is indirect, through SR load. The paper does not assign a direct sign, and neither does this record
sentence: In addition, STIM2 regulates Ca2+ movement through RyR1 during skeletal muscle contraction as well as SOCE.
justification: Recorded as unknown_regulation on purpose: the release channel responds, but through the pump rather than to the sensor, and inventing a sign would misrepresent the experiment. It sits beside STIM1 -> RYR1 inhibition from PMC6915709, which was measured on the coupling itself.
